answer: Each claim must grow a lotus rooted only in its own verified jobs, and pay 65 POA burned to plant it. Peers test it by hanging weight on the willow branch above it: a true lotus bends and holds, because its root is in the ledger. A copied lotus has no root, so it wilts under the first weight, the claim drops with its 65 POA burned, and the meadow stays closed to it. Cost doubles per claim from one operator, so 10 clones cost 66,495 POA; a lotus root is bound to its own ledger line and cannot be transplanted across identities.
